title: When AnimationTrack plays an animation in a loop, there will be a discontinuity when the animation restarts from the beginning.
body: ### Tested versions Godot Engine v4.5.1.stable.official.f62fdbde1 - https://godotengine.org Vulkan 1.4.312 - Forward+ - Using Device #0: NVIDIA - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1660 Ti ### System information Windows10 Godot Engine v4.5.1.stable.official.f62fdbde1 - https://godotengine.org Vulkan 1.4.312 - Forward+ - Using Device #0: NVIDIA - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1660 Ti ### Issue description I tried to use one AnimationPlayer to control another AnimationPlayer to create a cutscene animation, which includes loop-playing animation clips. Then I found that there is a discontinuity when the AnimationTrack is playing in a loop. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/def562ac-6b9e-4f20-928d-44e189a39270 And this phenomenon of incoherence is more obvious in Sprite animations, because Sprite animations cannot interpolate and are always discrete. ### Steps to reproduce ## Reporduce 1. Be sure to use Sprite + AnimationPlayer to create animations. And use 2D pixel character spritesheets. It is recommended to create relatively long animations, such as run and walk. But don not set run walk animation loop. Let AnimationTrack dirve it. 2. Then use another AnimationPlayer to create a test animation, set the animation to loop, and create an AnimationTrack for the sprite's AnimationPlayer in the animation. 3. Play run or walk in the AnimationTrack. Then you will see the following effect https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2842311b-4644-4fac-b68c-20b4b8496076 ## My Point I suspect that in the implementation of AnimationTrack, when the key of the starting frame is hit, AnimationTrack simply calls `AnimationPlayer.play`. The `AnimationPlayer.play` method has a characteristic: if the animation you want to play is already playing, then `play` will not restart the animation from the beginning. In the previous reproduction case, when the AnimationTrack loop hits the key of the starting frame for the second time, due to the processing order of the main loop, the AnimationPlayer may not have finished the currently playing animation yet. There might be an error of 1 frame? Therefore, the second call to `play` fails to restart the animation. Since the run and walk animations in the AnimationPlayer referenced by AnimationTrack are non-looping, the second round shows that the character is actually in the end state of the last frame of the animation. Finally, I came up with a temporary solution, which is to force a call to seek(0,0,true,false) at the starting frame of the AnimationTrack animation. Then you see, the loop animation is coherent. ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d6f31f2d-9e22-4b64-ac31-a6cabb3904ec) ## Summary I originally thought that the segments in AnimationTrack were a series of keys disguised as clips, but the truth seems to be that there is only one key. It calls the AnimationPlayer.play method and then renders it into a clip based on the animation length. Because of the behavioral characteristic of AnimationPlayer.play that if the target animation is already playing, calling play(target_anim) will not restart it from the beginning, coupled with the order of processing in the main loop, this may cause such discontinuities in AnimationTrack during looped animations. Calling seek directly on the starting frame is actually a temporary solution that doesn't address the root cause. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [animation_track_bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23728716/animation_track_bug.zip)
